recipes.title: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
recipes.dish_alt: Butter chicken in a creamy orange-red tomato sauce, served in a bowl
recipes.prep_alt: Marinated chicken thigh pieces searing in a pan

sections.heading: Steps
items: Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and mix with yogurt, half the ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, and half the Kashmiri chili powder. Marinate at least 20 minutes.
Sear the marinated chicken in hot oil 3-4 minutes per side until golden with charred spots. Set aside — it will finish cooking in the sauce.
Melt half the butter and cook the chopped onion 4-5 minutes until soft and see-through.
Stir in the remaining ginger-garlic paste 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add tomato passata, cashews, remaining chili powder, and a splash of water. Simmer 8-10 minutes until deep brick-red and oil separates at the edges.
Blend the sauce until completely smooth (let it cool first), then return it to the pan.
Return the seared chicken to the pan and simmer 8-10 minutes until no pink remains inside.
Stir in the sugar, remaining butter, and cream until the sauce turns lighter orange-red.
Crush the kasuri methi between your fingers and sprinkle it in with a final pinch of garam masala. Simmer 2 more minutes.
Taste, adjust salt and cream, and serve hot with basmati rice or naan.

recipes.title: Dal Tadka (Yellow Lentil Dal)
recipes.dish_alt: Golden yellow lentil dal topped with a sizzling tempering of cumin and chili
recipes.prep_alt: Cumin seeds and dried chili sizzling in ghee for the tadka

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Split yellow lentils (toor or moong dal)

sections.heading: Steps
items: Rinse the lentils until the water runs mostly clear, swishing and draining 2-3 times.
Bring the lentils, water, turmeric, and a pinch of salt to a boil, then simmer on low, lid slightly ajar.
Cook 20-25 minutes, skimming foam, until the lentils are completely soft and mushy.
Whisk the cooked dal until creamy and slightly thick, like a hearty soup.
Heat the ghee until a cumin seed sizzles right away when dropped in.
Add cumin seeds and dried chili, sizzling about 15 seconds until toasty, not black.
Add garlic 30 seconds until light golden, then onion 3-4 minutes until soft and browned at the edges.
Add the chopped tomato and cook 2-3 minutes until soft and pulpy.
Pour the sizzling tadka into the pot of dal, stir it in, taste for salt, and top with cilantro before serving.

recipes.title: Chicken Biryani (Hyderabadi-Style)
recipes.dish_alt: Layered chicken biryani with fried onions, mint, and saffron rice
recipes.prep_alt: Partially cooked basmati rice being layered over seared chicken

sections.heading: Steps
items: Marinate the chicken in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, half the garam masala, and salt for at least 30 minutes.
Rinse and soak the basmati rice 20-30 minutes so the grains cook up long and separate.
Boil water with bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and salt seasoned like seawater.
Add the drained rice and cook uncovered 5-6 minutes until about 70% cooked, then drain immediately.
Sear the marinated chicken in hot ghee 2-3 minutes per side until lightly browned.
Spread the seared chicken across the bottom of the pot.
Layer the partially cooked rice on top like a blanket, without stirring it in.
Sprinkle fried onions, mint, cilantro, remaining garam masala, and saffron milk over the rice.
Cover tightly and cook on very low heat 25-30 minutes without lifting the lid — this is the 'dum' steaming step.
Rest off heat, still covered, 10 minutes, then fluff and mix gently from the bottom up before serving.

recipes.title: Chana Masala (Chickpea Curry)
recipes.dish_alt: Chana masala chickpea curry in a thick tomato-based sauce
recipes.prep_alt: Ground spices toasting in oil with onion before the tomato goes in

sections.heading: Steps
items: Heat the oil and let the cumin seeds sizzle about 10 seconds until toasty.
Add the onion and cook 5-6 minutes, stirring often, until soft and golden-brown.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the ground coriander, cumin, turmeric, and chili powder, stirring 20 seconds to bloom the spices.
Add the tomato and cook 5-6 minutes, mashing it down, until it turns thick and jammy.
Add the chickpeas and water, stirring to coat every chickpea.
Simmer, partly covered, 10-12 minutes until the sauce thickens and the chickpeas soak up flavor.
Stir in the chana masala spice blend and amchur, then simmer 2 more minutes.
Sprinkle with cilantro and serve hot with rice, roti, or naan.

recipes.title: Paneer Tikka Masala
recipes.dish_alt: Seared paneer tikka masala in a creamy orange gravy with bell peppers
recipes.prep_alt: Marinated paneer, bell pepper, and onion searing with char spots in a pan

sections.heading: Steps
items: Cut the paneer, bell pepper, and onion into similar-sized chunks.
Mix yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, and half the garam masala into a marinade. Gently toss in the paneer and vegetables. Marinate 15-20 minutes.
Sear the marinated paneer and vegetables in a single layer, 2-3 minutes per side, until charred and softened. Set aside.
Melt the butter and cook the gravy onion 4-5 minutes until soft and see-through.
Add tomato passata and cashews, simmering 8-10 minutes until deepened and thickened.
Blend the sauce smooth (cool first), then return to the pan.
Stir in the cream, sugar, and remaining garam masala until the sauce turns soft orange.
Add the seared paneer and vegetables back in, simmering gently 3-4 minutes, stirring softly so the cubes stay whole.
Crush the kasuri methi over the top and stir in.
Taste, adjust salt, and serve hot with naan or rice.

recipes.title: Kerala Fish Curry
recipes.dish_alt: Kerala fish curry in a tangy coconut-milk sauce with curry leaves
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Tempering Mustard Seeds & Curry Leaves
recipes.prep_alt: Mustard seeds and curry leaves popping in hot coconut oil

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: White fish fillet (tilapia, cod, or snapper)

sections.heading: Steps
items: Pat the fish dry and rub with a pinch of turmeric and salt. Set aside.
Heat the coconut oil and add the mustard seeds — they'll pop and crackle within seconds.
Add the fenugreek seeds and curry leaves, frying about 10 seconds until fragrant and slightly crisp.
Add shallot, ginger, and garlic, cooking 3-4 minutes until soft and light golden.
Add the remaining turmeric, chili powder, and coriander, stirring 15 seconds to toast without burning.
Add the tomato and cook 2-3 minutes until it softens and breaks down.
Pour in the coconut milk and tamarind paste, bringing to a gentle simmer, not a hard boil.
Slide the fish into the curry in a single layer, cooking gently 6-8 minutes until opaque and flaking apart easily.
Taste and adjust salt or tamarind, then serve hot over steamed rice.

recipes.title: Lamb Rogan Josh
recipes.dish_alt: Deep red lamb rogan josh curry with whole warming spices
recipes.prep_alt: Marinated lamb chunks browning in a pot with whole spices

sections.heading: Steps
items: Mix the lamb with yogurt, Kashmiri chili powder, and ground fennel. Marinate at least 30 minutes, or overnight.
Heat the ghee and sizzle the bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves about 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add the onion and cook 6-8 minutes until deep golden-brown, lowering heat if it browns too fast.
Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the marinated lamb and cook 5-6 minutes until the outside turns gray-brown all over.
Pour in the water, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer, lid ajar.
Simmer 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lamb is fork-tender.
Taste and adjust salt. Fish out the whole spices before serving hot with rice or naan.

recipes.title: Gulab Jamun (Bonus)
recipes.dish_alt: Golden-brown gulab jamun balls soaking in cardamom syrup
recipes.prep_alt: Smooth dough balls frying gently in oil until deep reddish-brown

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Oil or ghee for deep frying

sections.heading: Steps
items: Make the syrup first: boil sugar, water, and crushed cardamom until dissolved, then simmer 5 minutes until slightly syrupy. Stir in rose water and set aside warm.
Combine milk powder, flour, and baking soda in a bowl.
Rub in the melted ghee until the mixture looks like damp sand.
Add milk a little at a time, kneading gently into a soft, smooth dough.
Roll the dough into small, smooth, crack-free balls.
Heat oil to medium-low — a pinch of dough should sink, then slowly float back up.
Lower the balls into the oil a few at a time, never crowding the pot.
Fry gently, rolling often, 6-8 minutes until deep reddish-brown all over.
Slide the fried balls directly into the warm syrup while still hot.
Let soak at least 30 minutes before serving warm or at room temperature.
